newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia plays down Castro role in troop release.
newsitem.headline: Colombia plays down Castro role in troop release.

text.p: President Ernesto Samper on Saturday played down reports that Colombia had asked Cuban leader Fidel Castro to mediate the release of 60 government troops held prisoner by Marxist guerrillas for three months.

He issued a statement saying that Colombia had explained details of the hostage crisis to Cuba and a number of other Latin American countries, and had asked them to urge the guerrillas to accept the government's terms. But he stressed that mediation efforts were being carried out by the International Committee of the Red Cross.

Reports about a possible role for Castro stemmed from comments by Foreign Relations Minister Maria Emma Mejia to the media, while attending a Caribbean development conference in Havana. Mejia said in a radio interview on Friday she felt Castro was "interested in making this humanitarian gesture" and she was confident he would help win the soldiers' freedom.

Samper said on Saturday, "We have not asked for any mediation because the mediation is being carried out by the International Committee of the Red Cross, which from the outset has played an excellent role."

"Rather than mediation what we have done is explain to several governments, including that of Cuba...the offer we have made to the guerrilla and have asked them in turn to ask the guerrillas to accept these terms," added the president.
The soldiers were seized by the Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) when it overran a jungle base in southern Putumayo province on Aug. 30.
Twenty-seven other soldiers were killed in the attack, which marked the start of one of the bloodiest guerrilla offensives in three decades of armed uprising.

Despite the government's agreement to demilitarize a large area of jungle in neighbouring Caqueta province for 10 days but the FARC demanded further areas be cleared and that the demilitarization period, due to expire on Monday night, be extended.
Castro was widely credited last June with winning the release of former Colombian President Cesar Gaviria's brother after his abduction by a leftist group called Dignity for Colombia.
